title: Does Order Matter? An Empirical Investigation into the Impact of File Ordering on Code Review Effectiveness
abstract: arXiv:2609.22610v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Modern code review is central to software quality, but its effectiveness depends on reviewer expertise, change characteristics, and how tools present changes. Most platforms display modified files alphabetically by default, although our prior work shows that developers find this ordering cognitively misaligned with how they understand multi-file pull requests. Whether these ordering-related attention patterns affect outcomes at scale remains unclear. We present a large-scale study of file ordering and review effectiveness, mining 330,343 multi-file pull requests and 756,814 file instances from 182 GitHub projects in five programming languages. We examine whether file position is associated with later bug-fixing changes, whether pull request size moderates this relationship, and whether reviewer attention, proxied by comments, aligns with latent bug outcomes. translated_title: 顺序重要吗？文件排序对代码评审有效性影响的实证研究
translated_abstract: 现代代码评审是软件质量的核心，但其有效性取决于评审者的专业知识、变更特征以及工具呈现变更的方式。大多数平台默认按字母顺序显示修改的文件，尽管我们之前的工作表明，开发者认为这种排序方式与他们理解多文件拉取请求的认知方式不一致。这些与排序相关的注意力模式是否会在大规模上影响评审结果仍不清楚。我们开展了一项关于文件排序与评审有效性的大规模研究，从五种编程语言的182个GitHub项目中挖掘了330,343个多文件拉取请求和756,814个文件实例。我们研究了文件位置是否与后续的缺陷修复变更相关、拉取请求的规模是否会调节这种关系，以及评审者的注意力（以评论为代理指标）是否与潜在的缺陷结果相一致。结果表明，文件位置之间存在统计显著但程度适中的关联。
tldr: 该论文通过对182个GitHub项目中33万多个多文件拉取请求的大规模实证研究，首次揭示了代码评审中文件的默认排序方式（如字母排序）与后续缺陷修复变更之间存在统计显著但适度的关联，表明文件呈现顺序可能影响代码评审的有效性。
en_tdlr: This paper presents a large-scale empirical study of over 330,000 multi-file pull requests from 182 GitHub projects, revealing statistically significant but modest associations between file ordering in code review and later bug-fixing changes, suggesting that file presentation order may impact code review effectiveness.
